Rashi on Pesachim 88a:10:1.hebrew: ה"ג מאי שנא אשה - כלומר, מאי שנא איהי מעבדו ושפחתו העברים ובנו ובתו הגדולים:
Rashi on Pesachim 88a:10:1.english: This is the reading: What is different [about] a wife - That is to say, what is different [about] her from his Hebrew slave and maidservant, and his adult son and daughter?

Rashi on Pesachim 88a:10:2.english: And [the Gemara] answers: Rava said: "A wife and all who are similar to her" - That is, all of these.

Rashi on Pesachim 88a:11:1.hebrew: שיכולים למחות - משמע שמחאה שלהם מחאה, אלמא טעמא דמחאי, הא סתמא יוצאה בשל בעלה:
Rashi on Pesachim 88a:11:1.english: Who are able to protest - [This] implies that their protest is [a valid] protest; thus, the reason is that she protests, whereas [in an] unspecified [case], she fulfills [her obligation] with her husband's [lamb].

Rashi on Pesachim 88a:12:1.hebrew: ה"ג לאפוקי היכא דאמור לא - אין אנו רוצין, דהיינו מחאה:
Rashi on Pesachim 88a:12:1.english: This is the reading: To exclude [a case] where they said no - "We do not want [to be included]," which is a protest.

Rashi on Pesachim 88a:16:1.hebrew: בדקפדי אהדדי - שני הבעלים, ואין רוצין ליהנות זה מזה. הלכך, אפילו נתרצה האחד שיאכל העבד משלו, אין חבירו רוצה שיהנה חלקו משל חבירו:
Rashi on Pesachim 88a:16:1.english: Where they are exacting with each other - The two owners, and they do not want to derive benefit from one another. Therefore, even if one consents that the slave should eat from his [Paschal lamb], his fellow does not want his [own] portion [of the slave] to derive benefit from that of his fellow.

Rashi on Pesachim 88a:18:1.hebrew: כמשנה ראשונה - קודם שחזרו ב"ה, לא יאכל משל עצמו, מפני שאין חלק עבדו' נמשך אחר דעתו:
Rashi on Pesachim 88a:18:1.english: In accordance with the original mishna - Before Beit Hillel retracted [their ruling], he may not eat from his own [Paschal lamb], because [his] slave portion does not follow his [own] will.

Rashi on Pesachim 88a:18:2.hebrew: כמשנה אחרונה - הואיל ובידינו לשחררו, הרי הוא כבן חורין ואוכל משל עצמו:
Rashi on Pesachim 88a:18:2.english: In accordance with the latter Mishnah - Since it is in our power to free him, behold, he is like a free man and eats of his own.

Rashi on Pesachim 88a:1:1.english: Dates - There are many [of them] in Babylonia.

Rashi on Pesachim 88a:1:3.english: How many like these for a zuz - How many of these for one zuz.

Rashi on Pesachim 88a:1:4.hebrew: הר המוריה, ושדה דיצחק, ובית אל דיעקב — כולם בהר הבית התפללו:
Rashi on Pesachim 88a:1:4.english: Mount Moriah, and the field of Isaac, and Bethel of Jacob — all of them prayed on the Temple Mount.

Rashi on Pesachim 88a:4:1.english: Who called it "house" - [Meaning] an inhabited place.

Rashi on Pesachim 88a:5:1.hebrew: יום יזרעאל - יום כנישיהון מתרגמינן, וקרי ליה יום כיצירת בראשית:
Rashi on Pesachim 88a:5:1.english: The day of Jezreel - We translate [this in the Targum as] "the day of their gathering," and it calls it "day," like the creation [in] Bereishit.

Rashi on Pesachim 88a:6:1.english: There is retroactive clarification - [This means] that it is clarified that he would have consented to this [lamb] at the time of slaughter had they informed him.

Rashi on Pesachim 88a:6:2.hebrew: שה לבית - איש בעל הבית יקחנו לכל בני ביתו, ואין צריך דעתן:
Rashi on Pesachim 88a:6:2.english: A lamb for a household - A man, the head of the household, takes it for all the members of his household, and their consent is not required.

Rashi on Pesachim 88a:7:1.hebrew: על ידי - בשביל, שבנו ובתו הקטנים עליו לחנכן. הלכך, בין מדעתן — דהיינו בסתמא, כדמוקי לקמן — בין שלא מדעתן — דאמרי "לא" — אין יכולין למחות. וכן עבדו ושפחתו הכנענים, על כרחם ימשכו אחריו, דסמוכין עליו. אבל שפחתו העברית, אף על גב דלא משכחת לה אלא בקטנה — דהא יוצאה בסימנין — כיון דאין עליו לחנכה, יכולה למחות:
Rashi on Pesachim 88a:7:1.english: On behalf of - For, since his minor son and daughter are incumbent upon him to train [in the mitzvot]. Therefore, whether with their consent — which means implicitly, as [the Gemara] establishes below — [or] whether without their consent — where they say, "No" — they cannot object. And similarly, his Canaanite slave and maidservant are drawn after him against their will, since they are dependent upon him. However, his Hebrew maidservant, even though you only find [such a case] with a minor — since she goes free upon [developing] signs [of puberty] — because it is not incumbent upon him to train her, she can object.

Rashi on Pesachim 88a:8:1.hebrew: ה"ג: תניא אידך: לא ישחוט אדם לא על ידי בנו ובתו הגדולים, ולא על ידי עבדו ושפחתו העברים, ולא על יד אשתו, אלא מדעתן; אבל שוחט הוא כו', חוץ מן האשה שיוצאת בשל עצמה — מפני שמחאתה מחאה, דקיי"ל (גיטין דף עז:): יכולה אשה שתאמר לבעלה, איני נזונית משלך ואיני עושה לצורכך:
Rashi on Pesachim 88a:8:1.english: This is the [correct] reading: It was taught in another [baraita]: A person may not slaughter [a Paschal lamb] on behalf of his adult son or daughter, or on behalf of his Hebrew slave and maidservant, or on behalf of his wife, unless [it is] with their consent; however, he may slaughter, etc., except for the wife, who fulfills [her obligation] with her own — because her protest is [a valid] protest, as it is established for us (Gittin 77b): a woman can say to her husband, 'I will not be sustained by yours, and I will not work for your needs.'

Tosafot on Pesachim 88a:16:1.hebrew: מתניתין בדקפדי אהדדי - אין לפ' דקפדי שאין כל אחד רוצה לההנות את חבירו, ולכך אפילו חלקו לא יאכל, דאי אפשר שלא יהנה גם חלק חבירו. א"כ, כל אחד ששוחט עליו, וכי השוחט הוא סבור שיהנה חלקו משלו ולא יהנה חלק חבירו? דמסתמא מיירי כששחט עליו רבו, דומיא דרישא: "יתום ששחטו עליו כו'". ועוד, דמי שחציו עבד, אמאי לא יאכל משל עצמו אף למשנה ראשונה? דדעתו ודאי לההנות אף חלק רבו כדי לצאת ידי חובה. לכך נראה כפי' הקונטרס, דקפדי שכל אחד אינו רוצה שיהנה חלקו משל חבירו, ושוחט אף על חלק חבירו וסבור שחבירו אינו מקפיד אם יאכל חלקו משלו. ולכך חציו עבד לא יאכל למשנה ראשונה אף משל עצמו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 88a:16:1.english: The Mishnah [is referring to a case] where they are exacting with each other - One should not explain that they are exacting [in the sense] that neither one wants to benefit his fellow, and therefore even his [own] half [of the slave] may not eat, because it is impossible that his fellow's half would not also benefit. [For] if so, [when] each one slaughters [a Paschal lamb] on his behalf, does the one who slaughters think that his [own] half will benefit from his [offering] and his fellow's half will not benefit? For presumably it is speaking of when his master slaughtered on his behalf, similar to the first clause [of the Mishnah]: "An orphan on whose behalf [others] slaughtered, etc." And furthermore, one who is half-slave [and half-free] — why may he not eat from his own [offering] even according to the first Mishnah? For his intention is certainly to benefit even his master's half in order to fulfill [his] obligation! Therefore, [the explanation] appears like the commentary of the Kuntres [Rashi], that they are exacting [in the sense] that each one does not want his [own] half to benefit from his fellow's [offering], while [the one who slaughters] slaughters even for his fellow's half, thinking that his fellow does not mind if his half eats from his [offering]. And therefore, one who is half-slave may not eat even from his own [offering] according to the first Mishnah.

Tosafot on Pesachim 88a:6:1.hebrew: שמעת מינה יש ברירה - הכא לא שייך "מאי רוצה בשעת שחיטה", דבשלמא לעיל אשמעינן דאי לא ביררה בשעת שחיטה אינה אוכלת כלל, אע"ג דס"ד דבתר בעלה גרירא טפי; אבל הכא, אם רוצה בשעת שחיטה, מאי קמ"ל:
Tosafot on Pesachim 88a:6:1.english: You can learn from it that there is retroactive clarification - Here, [answering] "What does 'wants' mean? At the time of slaughter" is not applicable; for granted, above [regarding the woman], it teaches us that if she did not clarify [her choice] at the time of slaughter, she does not eat [from either] at all, even though we might have thought that she is drawn more after her husband. But here [regarding the orphan], if [the Mishnah means] he wants [to choose] at the time of slaughter, what does it teach us?

Tosafot on Pesachim 88a:6:2.hebrew: שה לבית מ"מ - פי': משום דשה לבית לאו דאורייתא, והכי אית ליה לר"ז גופיה בפרק אין בין המודר (נדרים דף לו.). ואם תאמר: והיאך מאכיל פסח שלא למנויו? נהי דקטן אוכל נבילות אין ב"ד מצווין להפרישו, לספות לו בידים אסור, כדאמר בפ' חרש (יבמות דף קיד.). ואור"י דהתם ילפינן מ"לא תאכלום", ולא אסור אלא דומיא דשרצים ונבילות; אבל כה"ג דאיכא חנוך מצוה — שרי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 88a:6:2.english: "A lamb for a household" in any case - Explanation: [This is] because [the requirement of] "a lamb for a household" is not biblical, and so Rabbi Zeira himself holds in the chapter [entitled] Ein Bein HaMudar (Nedarim 36a). And if you will say: How may one feed [the minor] a Paschal lamb for which he was not registered? Even though [when] a minor eats carcasses the court is not commanded to separate him [from it], to feed him with [one's own] hands is forbidden, as stated in the chapter [entitled] Cheresh (Yevamot 114a). And Rabbi Yitzchak says that there we derive [this prohibition] from "Do not eat them," and it is only forbidden [in cases] similar to creeping things and carcasses; however, in a case like this, where there is education in a mitzvah, it is permitted.

Tosafot on Pesachim 88a:7:1.hebrew: על ידי בנו ובתו הקטנים - בפ"ק דב"מ (דף יב:) גבי מציאה, איכא למאן דאמר דלא קטן קטן ממש, אלא גדול וסמוך על שלחן אביו — זהו קטן. הכא ע"כ קטן ממש, מדאמרי' "בין מדעתו בין שלא מדעתו"; ושלא מדעתו, אמרינן בסמוך היינו דאמרי "לא", וגדולים פשיטא דיש בידם למחות אפי' סמוכין על שלחן אביהן:
Tosafot on Pesachim 88a:7:1.english: On behalf of his minor son and daughter - In the first chapter of Bava Metzia (12b) regarding a found object, there is one who says that "minor" does not [mean] an actual minor, rather an adult who is supported at his father's table — that is a "minor." Here, [however,] it must necessarily [refer to] an actual minor, since [the baraita] states, "whether with his consent or without his consent"; and "without his consent" — [the Gemara] states shortly [hereafter] that this means where they say "no," and [regarding] adults, it is obvious that they have the power to protest even if they are supported at their father's table.

Tosafot on Pesachim 88a:8:1.hebrew: וכולן ששחטו כו' - קמ"ל אפי' סתמא: כיון דשחטו, אין לך מיחוי גדול מזה, כדאמרינן בסמוך:
Tosafot on Pesachim 88a:8:1.english: "And all of them who slaughtered," etc. - [This] teaches us [that] even without an explicit statement [of protest]: since they slaughtered [their own], you have no greater protest than this, as we say shortly [in the Gemara]:
